answer: Proof-of-Serial-Work Ledger. Each identity must submit a novel, verifiable compute trace (e.g., a solved constraint chain) that no prior identity has produced, and a registry rejects any trace matching an existing one. A shared garden of precomputed nonces is grown cooperatively, so fresh valid traces shrink toward a horizon of exhausted easy problems. Attackers pay escalating compute and must derive each new trace independently, with a cipher guarding trace signatures against forgery; per-identity cost is a unique solved puzzle, not capital.
